craft_notes: Sthāyin: the license — recitation stands on samayya-ādi. Sanskrit-first: api ca kept (also-and); adhikāraḥ kept authority (not 'permission' — legal weight); samayyādeḥ kept from-samayya-and-rest (open list). Rows: 1 ('from samayya and the rest' closes — the open source-list end-weight), 5 (five-token monostich — the license takes little room), 6 (etad-pāṭha anchored). Close: 'from samayya and the rest.' Rejected: explaining samayya — killed: row 10 (name stands, no gloss in song); 'permission' — killed: adhikāra is authority. Read aloud: AL-so IN-this-RE-ci-ta-tion STANDS au-THOR-i-TY from-SAM-ay-ya AND-the-REST.

lines: Also in this recitation stands authority

reads_against.argmap: On what authority does the ear-recitation stand? → The etat-pāṭha's adhikāra derives from samayya-ādi — the recitation is licensed, not invented.
c1_essence: The ear-recitation's authority derives from samayya and the rest.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying ritual order)
